## Proposal: Set an H-1B Registration Intake Deadline of January 15

**The ask.** For this cap season, I'd like to set a firm internal intake deadline of **January 15** for H-1B registrations, with engagement letters and a one-page questionnaire going out to employer clients the week of December 7. Anything received after January 15 gets handled case by case. To be clear, this changes our own sequencing — it doesn't change what clients are expected to do.

**Why a set date.** Last season we filed 14 registrations for six employer clients, and nine of the 14 came in during the final week of February. Rosa logged roughly 11 hours of overtime the week the window opened. The cause is our process: today we email the questionnaire whenever an employer asks, so intake is whatever arrives and when. Nobody has been late to us — we haven't given anyone a date to be early to. One HR contact told me she would have sent everything in January if we'd asked. That's the framing I want to lead with.

**Why January 15 works for clients.** HR teams are back from holidays, budgets are set, and the $215 per-beneficiary registration fee is already budgeted in clients' Q1 plans. An earlier intake doesn't create new cost or new work for them; it gives them a clear date instead of an open request.

**Why it protects us.** The registration itself is simple, but the errors are expensive — a wrong passport means an invalid selection. We received a beneficiary's passport scan (Brightwater Analytics) two days before the window last season; it had expired in October, and the only reason we caught it was that Rosa checked the dates. A January deadline gives us room to verify rather than file and hope.

**What would actually change.**

- **Week of Dec 7:** engagement letters and one-page questionnaire go out to all employer clients.
- **Jan 15:** internal intake deadline.
- **Jan 15 – Feb 28:** Rosa owns the tracker and has a clean six weeks to chase gaps, verify documents, and confirm fees ahead of the March filing.
- **After Jan 15:** late requests reviewed case by case — nothing is declined, it's triaged as it arrives.
- **No change** to fees, filing work, or client commitments.

**Next step.** Marcus and I are sitting down Thursday to plan cap season. If he agrees, I can have the December letters out that week, so clients get the holidays plus January ahead of them.
